Your infrastructure matches the configuration.", and `az containerapp show` read the four cpu values on the new revision; the refusal of 2026-10-29 was the two-decimal precision rule (0.125), not a rule on values below 0.25

custom_domain_binding: yes: on 2026-10-29 the custom domain was bound by one apply with the proxied A record in place and the asuid TXT record; `az containerapp hostname list` reads bindingType SniEnabled with the certificate bound, and the environment certificate origin-certificate reads Succeeded, issuer CloudFlare Origin SSL Certificate Authority, expiring 2041-10-25; no DNS-only window was needed

edge_checks.note: the transform rule adds the origin header at the edge for every request to the host, so a request through Cloudflare never reaches the origin without it; the origin's own refusal (403) is read on the Ingress leg from the allowed developer address

ingress_origin_check.note: the 403 is the application's own refusal (the origin header check), not the ingress's allow-list refusal, which reads "RBAC: access denied"

allow_list_check.note: the ingress's own refusal: the allow-list (Cloudflare's published IPv4 ranges only) is in force again; the application is not reached

warm_window_started_at.read: az containerapp show --query properties.template.scale.minReplicas read 1 after the apply of min_replicas = 1 (plan app-12); the window ends with the apply that sets it back to 0

warm_window_ended_at.read: the time of the apply of plan app-13 (min_replicas 1 -> 0), recorded to the minute; az containerapp show --query properties.template.scale.minReplicas reads null after it (azurerm 5.11.0 sends no minimum when it is 0 (container_apps.go:1117); the service returns minReplicas null; the documented default minimum is 0 (scale-app)) and the Terraform state reads min_replicas 0

warm_window_allocation.read: az monitor activity-log list for the app (read 2026-11-12) holds no Microsoft.App/containerApps/write between the apply that opened the window (2026-11-03T02:17:06Z) and the apply that closed it (2026-11-05T21:56:45Z); the next write is the apply of plan app-14 (2026-11-06T02:02:25Z), which moved the replica from the fallback allocation, 1.0 vCPU and 2.0Gi, to 0.75 vCPU and 1.5Gi (sub_quarter_vcpu)

replicas_zero_after_window.read: az monitor metrics list --metric Replicas --aggregation Maximum --interval PT1M (read 2026-11-12) reads 1 for every minute from 21:50 through 22:02 and 0 for every minute from 22:03 through 22:29; the replica ran six minutes past the apply that closed the window, and those minutes are billed on the window's last day
